title: What he learned from Louis about preserving himself
summary: Watching Armstrong, Young learned to rest, not eat a big meal before playing, and not play too many high choruses at rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You were remarking this afternoon in rehearsal with Teddy Buckner that Louis wouldn't have done it that way.
No, Louis wouldn't have played that many high choruses at a rehearsal. He might have played one to see if he was in good shape, but he would have played the

others down, you know, preserve himself, you know. But he learned, Louis had to learn that too. But, you know, Louis had to -- it took time to learn that, for Louis to learn that too, but I learned a lot of things from Louis actually because I would watch him, you know, and I learned an awful lot watching Louis and listening to him, you know, because the guy had the experience, you know.
What particular things did you learn from Louis?

Well, one thing I learned from Louis was to -- how to preserve myself for a job. I learned also from Louis you never go out and have a big dinner and drinks and things before you go to work. All that came after work. And learned also you don't eat a big meal just before you go to play. Just like a swimmer, you know, you wouldn't eat a big meal, because the average wind, guy playing a wind instrument uses his diaphragm a lot; even a good singer would never go out and eat a big meal and go somewhere and sing because you can't breathe properly.

But these things I became more aware of when I was with Louis because he wouldn't do it. He just wouldn't do things like that, you know, and he always rested before he went to play. He relaxed before he went to a concert. You wouldn't catch him around doing a lot of autographing and things before he went to work. He -- that just wasn't his

style.
He'd autograph after work or in between or something like that, but -- in fact, he was protected in between concert -- like if you play a concert, they wouldn't let a lot of people come back and get autographs from Louie because they knew he had to prepare to go back for the next half.

Same way with Duke, any big star like that, but you watch them, these kind of people, and you learn, because they learned over the years. They made mistakes too, but they learned over the years. So why should you make a mistake? Why not watch them? And learn from them without going through all of that, you know. You -- what were you saying?
